the occurrence rate and creatine kinase enzyme activity of contact sites is changing during the stimulation of the heart by extracellular Ca.
the frequency of contact sites and the creatine kinase activity are changing according to the functional state of the heart.

the functional activity of Ca(2+) stimulated rat hearts and the formation of contact site and creatine kinase activities.
the question whether the functional activity of mitochondria is associated with the formation of mitochondrial contact sites.
the functional significance of the mitochondrial contact sites.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the formation of contact site is related to functional activity and thus efficient production of energy is provided.
the occurrence of contact sites and the associated creatine kinase activity are related to the functional status of the heart and that this relationship is mediated by Ca.
the formation of contact site and the creatine kinase activity are increased in the Ca stimulated rat hearts.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
contact sites are created by the fusion of the inner mitochondrial membrane with the outer mitochondrial membrane.
the contact site formation is a dynamic process and that this formation is related to energy production in the heart.
the formation of contact site and creatine kinase is induced by extracellular calcium in rat hearts.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the formation of mitochondrial contact sites in the Ca-stimulated rat heart is associated with increased creatine kinase activity.
mitochondrial contact sites and associated creatine kinase activity play a key role during the functional activity of Ca-stimulated rat heart.
the formation of contact site is related to the metabolic activity of the heart and thus efficient energy production is provided.
